messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — runtime node gpu-5 reporting repeated OOMs and container restarts. paged-attn allocator logs show growing 'fragmentation' metric and kvcache resident pages steadily increasing. Automatic fallback to model-small triggered. Investigate.

Alex: seeing same. GPU mem spikes at ~98% on longer sequences, but slow creep over hours. fragmentation_ratio trend from 0.12 -> 0.46 over 6h.

Priya: any customer-impact observed?

Sam: some requests hitting 504s at the edge around 03:12-03:20 UTC. error-rate up ~1.8% for hostpool region-us-west-2. Most are long-context chat sessions.

Maya: dumping allocator stats from node gpu-5: ```
# nvtop snapshot
GPU 0 mem 22.3G/24G
PagedAttnAllocator::stats {
  total_reserved: 34.2GB
  resident_pages: 12764
  fragmentation_ratio: 0.46
  stale_kv_pages: 942
}
```

Jordan: CUDA error shows sporadic "cuMemAlloc() failed: out of memory" in the runtime logs before container restart. Also seeing container OOMKilled from kube.

Alex: hypothesis: slow kvcache siphon where paged attention allocator keeps hoarding small page fragments that don't coalesce — gradual leak to OOM. Similar to earlier slow-drip incidents but this one's more noisy with node flaps.

Priya: immediate mitigation options? can we disable paging for heavy-encoder models on that pool, or force eviction policy more aggressively?

Sam: recommended: 1) cordon gpu-5, 2) scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes, 3) rollout fallback to model-compact for sessions > 8k tokens. Doing cordon now.

Maya: cordon applied to gpu-5. draining active pods with graceful 30s. migrating live requests to other nodes.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: rolled model-compact fallback to route 'chat-long' on us-west-2 canary 50% -> 100% in 2m.

Jordan: started heap scan script to compute slab occupancy and free-list lengths. Output: ```
slab 0: used 78% free-frag 22% fragments: 1432
slab 1: used 66% free-frag 34% fragments: 2601
kv-pages: 942 stale
```

Alex: TODOs: collect full allocator dump, trigger kv eviction compact, and if fragmentation persists, reboot container with clean cache. Need to confirm customer impact window and notify SRE on-call for reboot approval.

Priya: pinging accounts-team: potential exposed customers: acct-421 and acct-998 had elevated latency. Please open customer incident channel if we expect >30m.

Sam: I've opened a ticket INC-2026-847 and added the initial impact note. linking logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/runtime/gpu-5/5323456789

Maya: ran eviction compact command: ```
runtime-admin compact-kv --node gpu-5 --threshold 0.2 --force
``` returned: "compact started, reclaimed ~1.1GB"

Jordan: fragmentation ratio after compact down to 0.39. improvement but still above baseline. still seeing sporadic cuMemAlloc failures at lower frequency.

Alex: decision: keep node cordoned, leave fallback routes in place, schedule container restart during low-traffic window in 15m if no further improvements. standby for SRE approval.

OpsBot: incident-bot: SLO guard tripped for region-us-west-2: 99.5% -> 98.9% on p95 latency.

Priya: notifying on-call SRE @Jordan to approve a rolling restart of runtime pods on the affected pool. Jordan?

Jordan: approve. I'll coordinate a rolling restart with controlled concurrency 1 pod-at-a-time. we should preserve warm caches where possible; restart will clear kv caches though.

Maya: performing rolling restart now. command: ```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-pool-usw2 --selector=pool=dense-gpu --concurrency=1
```

Alex: live note — after first two restarts, fragmentation ratio on the remaining nodes slightly improved, and no new OOMKilled events. still monitoring.

Sam: customer-facing summary for now: partial degradation for long-context sessions in us-west-2 between 03:10-03:35 UTC. auto-fallback to smaller model prevented broader failures. We're actively mitigating; will post update in 20m. :thumbsup:

Priya: adding next-handoff info. oncall-junior shift starts in 2h. leaving detailed runbook steps: 1) check allocator fragmentation metric >0.4; 2) if >0.45 and compact reclaim <2GB in 30m -> escalate to oncall-sre; 3) consider node replace.

Jordan: postmortem notes to capture: root cause suspected gradual kvcache fragmentation interacting badly with paged-attn slab allocation under long-sequence workloads. recommends: defragmenter task, stronger periodic compaction, and eviction heuristics tuned to sequence-length telemetry.

Maya: final status update: node gpu-5 remains cordoned and reboot scheduled. p95 latency back to 99.6% and error-rate falling. I'll create a follow-up incident channel for postmortem.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated (active mitigations in place). next update at +1h or on change. :white_check_mark:

Sam: handing off to oncall-junior. key context: node gpu-5 cordoned, compaction run reclaimed ~1.1GB, rolling restarts in progress, fallback routes active. if OOMs reappear, escalate to eng-runtime and prepare node-replace.

Priya: thanks team. leaving timeline and logs in INC-2026-847. :eyes:

Jordan: thanks — will track postmortem and assign owners for defragmenter work.

Maya: handing over to next oncall. good luck. :coffee:
